newsitem.title: USA: Wash. state bill would define tribes as foreigners.
newsitem.headline: Wash. state bill would define tribes as foreigners.

text.p: Washington state legislators who want to ban foreign contributions to state political campaigns were including Indian tribes in their definition of foreigners, officials said on Wednesday.
"They're sovereign nations," Republican state Sen. Bob McCaslin said, employing a phrase tribes themselves use to describe their special legal status.

President Clinton's problems with improper foreign campaign contributions have focused attention on the fact that Washington state law is silent on foreign donations to state political campaigns. But the proposed legislative fix of the problem has provoked its own controversy.

"We're citizens. We've been citizens since 1928," fumed Native American political activist Russell LaFountaine of Seattle. "We have a right to look out for our interests and take part in the political process."
Tribal leaders elsewhere in the state said they were being targeted after emerging as a political and financial force in the last several elections.
Washington state tribes spent more than $2 million on campaigns in 1996, mostly to support an unsuccessful statewide ballot measure that would have legalised slot machine gambling in tribal casinos.
McCaslin argued that given voter concerns over campaign financing, "we ought to restrict (donations) down to those people in districts and within the state, and not sovereign nations and others."
The bill banning foreign and tribal campaign contributions has not yet been scheduled for a hearing.
